title: Impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on SAF Operations and Training
what_it_is: Impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on SAF Operations and Training

sections.label: Critical SAF operations continue
sections.summary: Critical SAF operations such as island defence, key installation protection, maritime security, air defence and counter-terrorism continue around the clock during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The SAF operations that are deemed critical such as island defence, protection of key installations, maritime security, air defence and counter-terrorism, continue around the clock even in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: MINDEF/SAF personnel mobilised
sections.summary: More than 6,000 MINDEF/SAF personnel were mobilised and deployed across national task forces and operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: More than 6,000 MINDEF/SAF personnel were mobilised and deployed across a wide range of national task forces and operations.

sections.label: Navy completes RIMPAC deployment
sections.summary: The Navy safely completed a 67-day deployment for RIMPAC, a multinational naval exercise held in Honolulu.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: For example, the Navy has just safely completed a 67-day deployment for the Rim of the Pacific, RIMPAC, which is a multinational naval exercise held in Honolulu.

sections.label: Air Force Darwin training deployment
sections.summary: Later this month the Air Force will deploy about 200 personnel and 10 aircraft to train in Darwin, Australia for about two months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Later this month, the Air Force will be deploying about 200 personnel and 10 aircraft to train in Darwin, Australia for about two months.

sections.label: Critical functions cannot stop
sections.summary: The assumption is that on an operational level, critical functions cannot stop.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our assumption is, as I had said, on an operational level, critical functions cannot stop.

sections.label: Overseas training and adjustments
sections.summary: Training overseas was done as much as possible, remaining training was done here with adjustments, and many army exercises were done in overseas areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have done everything possible to train as much as we can overseas, but what remains, has to be done here, we have done it and we have made adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But for a lot of the army exercises, tanks, artilleries, our HIMARS operations, our infantry and so on and so forth, we have done that in overseas areas.

sections.label: Local training and mass testing
sections.summary: The speaker says local training will continue and be stepped up, and that mass testing is needed to train at the desired tempo and pace locally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Be that as it may, where we can, we will continue and step up local training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: That is why, I mentioned that, in order for us to give us the confidence to be able to train at the tempo and at the pace that we want to, even locally, our assessment is that we will need mass testing.

sections.label: Acceptable accurate testing methods
sections.summary: The speaker says tests must be acceptable and accurate, citing saliva and oropharyngeal mid-turbinate testing for larger groups and other innovative methods being worked on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The way to do that is to have tests which are acceptable, which are accurate and that is why I mentioned saliva testing, I mentioned oropharyngeal mid-turbinate testing, which can be more readily applied to larger groups, as well as other innovative methods of testing that we are working on.
